picks.title: I Feel Sad and Mad Because I Keep Repeating the Same Emotional Patterns — The Emotional Growth That Helped Me Break Free from a Powerless Way of Living, Trust My Higher Power, and Live with Faith and Oneness
picks.summary: Why do the same relationships, emotional reactions, and painful patterns keep showing up, even when you thought you had already healed?In this episode of WE, Joe Mittiga explores his belief that our biggest emotional reactions can reveal unresolved pain within us. picks.reason: Explores emotional patterns, faith, and personal responsibility for growth.

picks.showTitle: The Bible in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)
picks.title: Day 265: Sins of Omission (2026)
picks.summary:
Fr. Mike explains sins of omission, and how these are some of the biggest deciding factors of who goes to heaven and who goes to hell: whether or not we did good works God called us to. He also reminds us that not all of the New Testament parables are universally relevant, recalling the parable of the talents and the parable of the wise and foolish maidens. Today's readings are Matthew 25-26 and Proverbs 19:21-24.

For the complete reading plan, visit ascensionpress.com/bibleinayear.

picks.title: Does Consciousness Break the Laws of Physics?
picks.summary: If we could explain everything happening in your brain, would there still be something left to explain about you? Physicist Avshalom Elitzur thinks so—and argues that accounting for consciousness may require changing the laws of physics. In this lively conversation, Michael Shermer challenges Elitzur on why subjective experience should be anything more than a product of the brain, whether an AI could be conscious, and what a hypothetical human without consciousness would have to say about any of this. Avshalom Elitzur is an Affiliate Professor at the Institute for Quantum Studies, Chapman Univ
picks.reason: A serious discussion on consciousness and physics, questioning subjective experience.

picks.title: Saturated Saturday: When God Doesn’t Do What You Think He Should — Pastor Jason Shepperd
picks.summary:
What happens to your faith when God doesn’t do what you think a good God should do?
The gospel doesn’t promise a life without pain. It gives us hope in the middle of it. In 2 Samuel 12, David faces unimaginable loss and has a decision to make: will his pain cause him to stop seeking God, or lead him into deeper trust and surrender?
Grace doesn’t disappear when pain enters our lives, and God’s character doesn’t change when our circumstances do.The gospel includes suffering, but it ends in resurrection. Because the tomb is empty, pain does not get the final word.

picks.reason: A pastor reflects on faith and suffering through David's story in 2 Samuel 12.
